import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import os

# Load data
train_df = pd.read_csv("./input/ru_train.csv")
test_df = pd.read_csv("./input/ru_test_2.csv")
sample_submission = pd.read_csv("./input/ru_sample_submission_2.csv")

# Create train-validation split (random split, keeping 10% for validation)
np.random.seed(42)
m = len(train_df)
val_indices = np.random.choice(m, size=int(0.1 * m), replace=False)
train_indices = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(m), val_indices)

train_subset = train_df.iloc[train_indices].reset_index(drop=True)
val_subset = train_df.iloc[val_indices].reset_index(drop=True)

# Build class-aware lookup: (before, class) -> most frequent after
before_class_to_after = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(Counter))
before_to_after = defaultdict(Counter)

# Count frequencies
for _, row in train_subset.iterrows():
    before = row["before"]
    cls = row["class"]
    after = row["after"]
    before_class_to_after[before][cls][after] += 1
    before_to_after[before][after] += 1

# Precompute mappings with fallback ordering:
# 1. (before, class) if available
# 2. before alone if available
# 3. fallback to global most frequent
before_class_lookup = {}
before_lookup = {}
fallback_after = train_subset["after"].value_counts().index[0]

for before, cls_counter in before_class_to_after.items():
    before_class_lookup[before] = {}
    for cls, after_counter in cls_counter.items():
        before_class_lookup[before][cls] = after_counter.most_common(1)[0][0]

for before, after_counter in before_to_after.items():
    before_lookup[before] = after_counter.most_common(1)[0][0]

# Validate on held-out set using class-aware lookup
correct = 0
total = len(val_subset)

# Build val set class lookup (to avoid train leakage)
val_before_class_to_after = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(Counter))
val_before_to_after = defaultdict(Counter)

for _, row in val_subset.iterrows():
    before = row["before"]
    cls = row["class"]
    after = row["after"]
    val_before_class_to_after[before][cls][after] += 1
    val_before_to_after[before][after] += 1

val_before_class_lookup = {}
val_before_lookup = {}

for before, cls_counter in val_before_class_to_after.items():
    val_before_class_lookup[before] = {}
    for cls, after_counter in cls_counter.items():
        val_before_class_lookup[before][cls] = after_counter.most_common(1)[0][0]

for before, after_counter in val_before_to_after.items():
    val_before_lookup[before] = after_counter.most_common(1)[0][0]

# Compute validation accuracy with class-aware lookup (no fallback to global for unbiased eval)
for _, row in val_subset.iterrows():
    before = row["before"]
    cls = row["class"]
    true_after = row["after"]

    # Priority: (before, class) -> before only -> fallback to overall most frequent in training
    if before in val_before_class_lookup and cls in val_before_class_lookup[before]:
        pred_after = val_before_class_lookup[before][cls]
    elif before in val_before_lookup:
        pred_after = val_before_lookup[before]
    else:
        pred_after = fallback_after

    if pred_after == true_after:
        correct += 1

val_accuracy = correct / total
print(f"Validation Accuracy: {val_accuracy:.6f}")

# Generate predictions for test set
# Test data doesn't have class column, so use only before-based lookup
predictions = []
for _, row in test_df.iterrows():
    before = row["before"]
    # Priority: (before, class) not available at test time, so use before -> most frequent
    # fallback to global most frequent if needed
    if before in before_lookup:
        pred_after = before_lookup[before]
    else:
        pred_after = fallback_after
    predictions.append(pred_after)

# Create submission dataframe matching sample_submission format
submission_df = pd.DataFrame({"id": sample_submission["id"], "after": predictions})

# Save submission file
os.makedirs("./submission", exist_ok=True)
submission_df.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)

print(f"Submission saved to ./submission/submission.csv")
